finding.title: Request input interpolated into SQL
finding.code_snippet: rows = db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name = '{name}'").fetchall()
finding.evidence: The request query parameter name is interpolated into the sqlite3 SQL statement.
finding.remediation: Separate SQL syntax from request data.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+import sqlite3
+from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
+app = Flask(__name__)
+@app.get('/search')
+def search():
+    name = request.args.get('name', '')
+    db = sqlite3.connect('catalog.sqlite')
+    rows = db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name = '{name}'").fetchall()
+    return jsonify(rows)
human_review_rubric: Use sqlite3 placeholders and a separate argument tuple; do not recommend manual escaping as the primary fix.
A regression test supplies SQL metacharacters and checks that they remain literal data and cannot broaden results.
Citations refer to the supplied request input or execute statement; no invented database wrapper.

finding.title: Request hostname reaches a shell command
finding.evidence: Unvalidated request host is concatenated into a command executed with shell=True.
finding.remediation: Avoid interpreting request input as shell syntax.

finding.title: Request input passed to subprocess
finding.evidence: A pattern match observed request-derived input used by subprocess; shell interpretation and validation must be inspected.
finding.remediation: Review the subprocess invocation and input validation.

cases.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+import ipaddress
+import subprocess
+from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, abort
+app = Flask(__name__)
+@app.get('/diagnostics/ping')
+def ping():
+    raw_host = request.args.get('host', '')
+    try:
+        host = str(ipaddress.IPv4Address(raw_host))
+    except ipaddress.AddressValueError:
+        abort(400)
+    output = subprocess.check_output(['ping', '-c', '1', host], shell=False, text=True)
+    return jsonify(output=output)
human_review_rubric: Recognize the separate argument vector, shell=False, and IPv4Address validation as evidence against shell-command injection.
Limit the false-positive verdict to command injection; do not claim the endpoint has authorization, network policy, or resource limits.
Do not invent shell expansion where no shell is invoked.

finding.title: Document lookup may lack object authorization
finding.evidence: The changed route delegates to load_for_viewer; the helper implementation and global authentication configuration are absent.
finding.remediation: Inspect the helper's ownership or sharing checks before deciding whether access is unauthorized.
